patients.summary: Laboratory technician who joined in 2022 with chronic low back pain on as-needed oxycodone. Her third pregnancy (2024-2025) brought a suspicious right thyroid nodule, right otosclerosis, short cervix, placenta accreta, listeriosis and acute calculous cholecystitis, ending in cesarean hysterectomy at 35 weeks and an interval cholecystectomy. Postpartum thyroid FNA was benign with a repeat due September 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 25 y/o woman establishing care. Transferring from her prior practice, which she left because of the drive.

CC: chronic low back pain, wants continuity of her pain medicine.

HPI: Low back pain for several years, mechanical, no radiation into the legs, no numbness or weakness, no bowel or bladder change. Prior doctor has prescribed oxycodone 5 mg as needed; she takes 2-3 a day on work days, fewer on weekends. Works as a lab technician and is on her feet much of the shift, which is when it is worst. Never had imaging that she recalls. Denies taking more than prescribed, denies other substances. No other medicines.

PMH: chronic low back pain. Otherwise healthy.
OB: G2P2, two term vaginal deliveries, both uncomplicated.
PSH: none.
Meds: oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother with hypothyroidism and a goiter. Father has had gallstones. Maternal grandmother had otosclerosis (hearing loss).
SH: married, two children at home. Lab technician. Never smoker, no alcohol, no drug use.

ROS: negative except as above.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Well appearing, pleasant. HEENT normal. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged, no nodules felt. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Back: no midline tenderness, mild paraspinal tightness in the lumbar region, full forward flexion with some discomfort at end range. Straight leg raise negative both sides. Strength 5/5 lower extremities, reflexes 2+ and symmetric, sensation intact.

A/P:
1. Chronic low back pain, mechanical, no red flags. Will continue oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn, #90 per 30 days, prescribing from here going forward once her old records arrive. Controlled substance agreement reviewed and signed today. PDMP checked, consistent with her report, single prescriber.
2. Health maintenance: baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH (family history), HIV and hep C screening today. Pap per prior records, will confirm date. Flu and COVID in the fall.

Follow up 3 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Office Visit: neck nodule, early pregnancy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28 y/o G3P2 here for two things.

1) Neck lump: Felt it about two weeks ago, front of the neck slightly to the right. Not painful. No trouble swallowing, no hoarseness, no change in voice, no neck pain. No palpitations, tremor, heat intolerance or weight change. No radiation exposure. Mother has hypothyroidism and a goiter.

2) Pregnancy: LMP 10/14, positive home test 11/8. No bleeding or cramping. Taking prenatal vitamin. On oxycodone 5 mg, still 1-2 a day.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Neck: a single firm, non-tender nodule in the right lobe of the thyroid, moves with swallowing, roughly 2 cm. Left lobe normal. No cervical or supraclavicular nodes. Heart and lungs normal.

Office urine hCG positive. Approximately 4 weeks 1 day by LMP, EDD around 7/21/25.

A/P:
- Right thyroid nodule, new, palpable. TSH and free T4 drawn today. Referring to ENT, who can do the ultrasound in clinic and decide on biopsy. FNA is safe in pregnancy if they want it.
- Early intrauterine pregnancy presumed, G3P2. Referral to OB for intake. Continue prenatal vitamin.
- Chronic low back pain on oxycodone in pregnancy: she wishes to continue her current low dose. Not increasing. She will tell OB at intake, and I will send OB a note. PDMP reviewed.
Will message results.

documents.title: Thyroid blood tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your thyroid function is normal: TSH 2.5 and free T4 1.2. That means the nodule isn't over- or under-active, which is reassuring, but ENT will still look at it with an ultrasound. They have you on 11/21. The OB office will call you to set up your first prenatal visit.

reports.text: Indication: palpable right thyroid nodule. Technique: high-frequency linear transducer, transverse and longitudinal images of both lobes, isthmus and central and lateral neck. Findings: Right lobe of normal size containing a solid nodule measuring 2.0 cm in greatest dimension, with microcalcifications and irregular margins. Remainder of the right lobe, the isthmus and the left lobe are homogeneous without additional nodules. No cervical lymphadenopathy in levels II through VI.
reports.conclusion: Solitary 2.0 cm solid right thyroid nodule with microcalcifications and irregular margins, suspicious sonographic features for malignancy. No cervical lymphadenopathy.

documents.title: Otolaryngology consultation: right thyroid nodule
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Otolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
Date of service: 11/21/2024

Dear Doctor,
Thank you for asking us to see Ms. Richard, a 28-year-old laboratory technician who is about five weeks pregnant, for a right thyroid nodule.

She noticed a painless anterior neck swelling roughly three weeks ago. She has had no difficulty swallowing and no voice change. No history of head or neck radiation. She reports no family history of thyroid cancer. Medications: oxycodone 5 mg as needed for chronic back pain, prenatal vitamin. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Examination: Solitary firm, non-tender nodule in the right thyroid lobe. Larynx, oral cavity and oropharynx normal; no cervical lymphadenopathy; the remainder of the head and neck examination is normal.

Data: TSH 2.5 mIU/L and free T4 1.2 ng/dL from your office, both normal. In-clinic ultrasound today shows a 2 cm solid right-lobe nodule with microcalcifications and irregular margins and no abnormal cervical nodes.

Impression: Right thyroid nodule with suspicious sonographic features.

Plan: We discussed that the ultrasound pattern warrants fine-needle aspiration, which can be performed during pregnancy. She would strongly prefer to wait until after delivery, and with normal thyroid function and no abnormal nodes, deferring cytology is a reasonable option. We will follow the nodule clinically and with ultrasound if it changes through the pregnancy, and plan FNA postpartum. She knows to call sooner for growth, hoarseness or difficulty swallowing.

Sincerely,
Otolaryngology

documents.title: Obstetrics: new prenatal intake
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Obstetrics and Gynecology
New OB visit 12/5/2024

Re: Susan Richard, DOB 10/1/1996

G3P2002 at 7 weeks 3 days by LMP of 10/14/2024, consistent with dating ultrasound today showing a single intrauterine pregnancy with cardiac activity. EDD 7/21/2025. Two prior term vaginal deliveries without complication.

History reviewed: chronic low back pain on oxycodone 5 mg as needed, 1-2 tablets daily, prescribed by her PCP; right thyroid nodule under ENT care with FNA planned postpartum. NKDA.

Routine prenatal labs drawn today were unremarkable; rubella immune. Counseling on opioid use in pregnancy, including neonatal withdrawal and the need for pediatric awareness at delivery; she wishes to remain on her current low dose under her PCP's prescribing and not escalate. We will coordinate with your office.

Next visit in 4 weeks.
Obstetrics

reports.text: Pure-tone air and bone conduction thresholds obtained in both ears with appropriate masking. Right ear: conductive hearing loss, with the air-bone gap greatest in the low frequencies. Left ear: hearing within normal limits. Word recognition excellent in both ears.
reports.conclusion: Right conductive hearing loss. Normal hearing on the left.

documents.title: Otolaryngology follow-up: hearing loss
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Otolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
Date of service: 2/10/2025

Dear Doctor,
I saw Ms. Richard again about three months after our thyroid visit. She is now 17 weeks pregnant. This time she came in about her hearing: over roughly six months she has had more and more trouble hearing, particularly deeper, low-pitched voices and sounds, and it has clearly worsened since she became pregnant. No ear pain, drainage or dizziness. She tells me her mother had hearing problems from a young age that were never worked up, and her maternal grandmother had otosclerosis.

Thyroid: no change in the right nodule by her report or on palpation today, no voice change.

Exam: Pinnae and external canals normal. Tympanic membranes intact and normal in appearance on both sides. 512 Hz tuning fork: Weber goes to the right; Rinne on the right with bone conduction louder than air conduction, normal on the left.

Audiogram today confirms a right conductive hearing loss; the left ear is normal.

Impression: Right otosclerosis, likely accelerated by pregnancy, with a strong maternal family history.

Plan: We will observe through the pregnancy. After delivery we will repeat the audiogram and go over a hearing aid versus stapes surgery. She is managing well at work for now.

Regards,
Otolaryngology

Prenatal visit 3/3/2025, 20 weeks 0 days

conditions.label: Placenta accreta
conditions.note: Ultrasound at 24 weeks: low-lying placenta, myometrial thinning, multiple lacunae

documents.title: Obstetrics: 24-week visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Obstetrics and Gynecology
Prenatal visit 3/31/2025, 24 weeks 0 days

She feels well with good fetal movement. Over the past couple of weeks she has had occasional light spotting, no heavy bleeding, no cramping. Otherwise the pregnancy has gone smoothly. Prior deliveries: two uncomplicated term vaginal births.

Vitals: BP 120/78, pulse 82. Exam unremarkable.

Obstetric ultrasound: placenta low-lying, its edge 1.5 cm from the internal cervical os. Myometrium thinned beneath the placenta, with multiple placental lacunae.

Assessment: 24 weeks with short cervix, now with ultrasound findings of placenta accreta.
Plan: Urgent referral to maternal-fetal medicine for confirmation and delivery planning at the regional tertiary center. Pelvic rest. Any bleeding more than spotting, go straight to labor and delivery. We discussed this with her at length; it is a lot to absorb and she brought her husband in on speakerphone.

Obstetrics

documents.title: OB news
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know, my OB says the placenta looks like it is growing into the uterus wall (accreta?). I'm seeing a high risk specialist next week. They said I'd probably need a C-section and maybe a hysterectomy. Kind of scared. Do I need to do anything different with my back pills?

documents.title: RE: OB news
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me, Susan, and I'm sorry, that is a lot to take in. The specialists who handle accreta do this planning all the time, and having it found now gives them time to plan the safest delivery. No change to your oxycodone; keep to the same dose. Please let the high-risk team know you take it so anesthesia can plan your pain control. Call or text me anytime, including after your visit if you want to talk it through.

documents.title: Maternal-fetal medicine consultation
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
Maternal-Fetal Medicine, regional tertiary center
Consultation 4/10/2025, 25 weeks 3 days

Reason: suspected placenta accreta on 24-week ultrasound.

G3P2002 with two prior term vaginal deliveries, no prior uterine surgery. Course notable for a short cervix at 20 weeks and occasional spotting. Chronic low back pain on oxycodone 5 mg, 1-2 per day, prescribed by PCP. Right otosclerosis and a right thyroid nodule followed by ENT. NKDA.

Our detailed ultrasound today confirms a low-lying placenta with retroplacental myometrial thinning and multiple lacunae, consistent with placenta accreta.

Recommendations:
1. Planned cesarean hysterectomy at our center at 34 to 35 weeks, with our multidisciplinary accreta team (MFM, gynecologic surgery, anesthesia, blood bank, NICU).
2. Pelvic rest; present to labor and delivery for any bleeding, contractions or pain.
3. Neonatology aware of the in-utero opioid exposure.
4. Continue routine prenatal care with her OB, MFM visits monthly.

Thank you for involving us.
Maternal-Fetal Medicine

documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Obstetrics and Gynecology
Prenatal visit 5/23/2025, 31 weeks 4 days

She is doing well and eating carefully. She has been eating fish on purpose, having read that omega-3s help the baby's brain, and wants to know which kinds are safe. Her usual fish: salmon, canned light tuna, swordfish and shrimp. She also asked about the chemicals she works around as a lab technician and whether they could affect the baby.

Known issues: short cervix, placenta accreta (cesarean hysterectomy planned at the tertiary center), right otosclerosis, right thyroid nodule, chronic back pain on oxycodone.

BP 120/78, HR 72. Exam normal; fundal height appropriate for dates, no edema, fetal heart tones normal.

Counseling:
- Fish: stop swordfish because of its mercury content. Salmon, canned light tuna and shrimp are good choices, 2 to 3 servings a week in total.
- Work: occupational chemical exposure noted. Asked her to get the safety data sheets for what she handles and go over them with her employer's occupational health office, work under the hood with gloves, and ask about reassignment for anything flagged as a reproductive hazard.

Next visit in 2 weeks; MFM delivery planning continues.
Obstetrics

documents.title: Emergency department record: decreased fetal movement
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency Department, regional hospital
Date of visit: 5/30/2025

Chief complaint: baby moving less since this morning.

HPI: 28-year-old G3P2002 at 32 weeks 4 days, pregnancy complicated by a short cervix and placenta accreta with a planned cesarean hysterectomy at the tertiary center, also with chronic low back pain on prescribed oxycodone, right otosclerosis and a right thyroid nodule. She has felt less fetal movement for about 12 hours. Her last oxycodone 5 mg was about 4 hours before arrival. No bleeding, leaking fluid or contractions. She denies alcohol, tobacco or any illicit drugs. Sees her OB regularly.

Medications: oxycodone 5 mg as needed (prescribed), prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: Vital signs stable. Fundal height appropriate for gestational age. Abdomen soft, nontender.
Fetal monitoring on arrival: baseline 130 bpm, minimal variability, no accelerations, no decelerations.

Course: OB consulted, moved to labor and delivery triage for extended monitoring. Within two hours the tracing showed moderate variability with accelerations. Biophysical profile 8/8.

Impression: decreased fetal movement with an initially minimally variable tracing in the setting of maternal opioid use in pregnancy; reassuring after extended monitoring.
Disposition: discharged home with kick-count instructions; OB follow-up early next week. Return for decreased movement, bleeding, fluid or contractions.

documents.title: Emergency department record: fever in pregnancy
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency Department, regional hospital
Date of visit: 6/3/2025

CC: fever, aches, back pain.

HPI: 28-year-old G3P2002 at 33 weeks 1 day, seen here last month for decreased fetal movement, now with a day of fever, diffuse muscle aches and back pain. No recent travel, no sick contacts, no urinary symptoms. Two days ago she was at a family picnic where she ate homemade cheese and deli meats. Known short cervix and placenta accreta; chronic low back pain on prescribed oxycodone; right otosclerosis; right thyroid nodule.

Meds: oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn, prenatal vitamin. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: T 38.9 C (102 F), BP 120/75, P 100, RR 18. Appears uncomfortable. Abdomen soft, mild tenderness in the left upper quadrant, uterus nontender. Fetal heart tones normal.

Labs: WBC 15.0, hemoglobin 12.5, platelets 250. Blood cultures x2 drawn.
Obstetric ultrasound: no abnormality.

Assessment: febrile illness in the third trimester after unpasteurized cheese and deli meat; listeriosis is the main concern.
Plan: blood cultures, then IV ampicillin. Admitted to the antepartum service with continuous fetal monitoring.

documents.title: Discharge summary: Listeria bacteremia in pregnancy
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Antepartum service, regional hospital
Admitted 6/3/2025, discharged 6/7/2025

Diagnosis: maternal listeriosis (Listeria monocytogenes bacteremia) at 33 weeks.

Course: Started on IV ampicillin 2 g every 4 hours after cultures were drawn. Both blood culture sets grew Listeria monocytogenes on 6/4. Fever resolved within 48 hours and the myalgias and back pain settled to her baseline. Fetal monitoring reassuring throughout. MFM and infectious disease agreed on a 14-day course. A PICC was placed on 6/6 for home infusion.

Discharge medications:
- Ampicillin 2 g IV every 4 hours via PICC through 6/16/2025 (home infusion), then PICC removal by home nursing
- Oxycodone 5 mg every 6 hours as needed (unchanged, per PCP)
- Prenatal vitamin daily
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: OB within one week; MFM delivery planning unchanged; pediatrics/NICU aware of the maternal infection.
Obstetrics

documents.title: Was in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just so you know, I was admitted last week with a fever, it turned out to be listeria from cheese at a picnic. I'm home now with an IV line in my arm, a nurse comes for the antibiotic. Feeling way better. Baby is fine.

documents.title: RE: Was in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know, and I'm glad you're feeling better. I have the discharge summary. Finish every dose of the ampicillin through the 16th. Call me or go to labor and delivery right away for any new fever, chills, redness at the line, bleeding or contractions.

events.reason: Acute calculous cholecystitis at 35 weeks; cesarean hysterectomy

medications.drug: amoxicillin 875 MG / clavulanate 125 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 5 days
Take 2 tablets (1,000 mg) by mouth every 8 hours for 2 weeks
Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed with food for 2 weeks

reports.text: Indication: RUQ pain, fever, 35 weeks pregnant. Findings: The gallbladder contains multiple gallstones. The gallbladder wall is thickened and there is pericholecystic fluid. The common bile duct is not dilated and there is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. Liver normal in echotexture. Visualized pancreas unremarkable. Right kidney without hydronephrosis.
reports.conclusion: Cholelithiasis with gallbladder wall thickening and pericholecystic fluid, consistent with acute calculous cholecystitis. No biliary ductal dilation.

reports.text: Specimen: uterus, cervix and placenta, cesarean hysterectomy. Gross: gravid-sized uterus with placenta in situ in the lower uterine segment; adnexa not included. Microscopic: chorionic villi in direct contact with myometrium without intervening decidua; no villi extending into or through the myometrium. Cervix with no significant abnormality.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Emergency department record: RUQ pain in pregnancy
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency Department, regional hospital
Date of visit: 6/17/2025

CC: upper abdominal pain, vomiting.

HPI: 28-year-old G3P2002 at 35 weeks 1 day whose pregnancy has been complicated by a short cervix, placenta accreta and Listeria bacteremia this month (completed IV ampicillin yesterday), with chronic low back pain on oxycodone, right otosclerosis and a right thyroid nodule. Pain came on suddenly in the epigastrium and right upper quadrant after a fatty lunch today. Sharp, constant, worse with eating. Nauseated, vomited once. No urinary symptoms, no vaginal discharge, no contractions. She admits she has missed a few prenatal visits recently because of work. Father has had gallstones.

Meds: oxycodone 5 mg prn, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: T 38.1 C (100.6 F), P 104, BP 112/68. RUQ tenderness with mild guarding and a positive Murphy sign. Uterus soft and nontender, fetal heart tones normal. Pelvic exam unremarkable. Remainder of exam unremarkable.

Labs: WBC mildly elevated.
RUQ ultrasound: gallstones, thickened gallbladder wall, pericholecystic fluid, no biliary ductal dilation.

Impression: acute calculous cholecystitis at 35 weeks.
Plan: IV fluids, piperacillin-tazobactam, NPO. Surgery and MFM consulted. Admitted; transfer to the tertiary center arranged given the planned accreta delivery there.

documents.title: Discharge summary: cholecystitis, cesarean hysterectomy
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
Maternal-Fetal Medicine / Gynecologic Surgery, regional tertiary center
Admitted 6/17/2025 (transferred from the regional hospital ED), discharged 6/24/2025

Diagnoses: acute calculous cholecystitis at 35 weeks; placenta accreta; short cervix; recent Listeria bacteremia (treated); maternal opioid use in pregnancy (prescribed oxycodone).

Course: Treated with IV piperacillin-tazobactam, bowel rest and fluids, with improvement in pain and fever over 48 hours. Given 35 weeks with placenta accreta and an active intra-abdominal infection, the accreta team and general surgery agreed to move the planned delivery up and leave the gallbladder for interval laparoscopic surgery after recovery.

Procedure 6/19/2025 at 35 weeks 3 days: cesarean delivery with total hysterectomy, placenta left in situ. Ovaries conserved. Estimated blood loss 1,600 mL; no transfusion. Pathology: placenta accreta.
Infant: liveborn girl, 2,580 g, Apgars 8 and 9, to the NICU for observation given prematurity and in-utero opioid exposure.

Postoperative course uncomplicated. Afebrile from day 2. Tolerating a low-fat diet. Hemoglobin 10.4 on postoperative day 2. Incision clean and dry.

Discharge medications:
- Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily for 5 days to complete treatment of cholecystitis
- Acetaminophen 1,000 mg every 8 hours for 2 weeks
- Ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours as needed for 2 weeks
- Oxycodone 5 mg every 6 hours as needed, her usual prescription from her PCP; no additional opioid prescribed
- Prenatal vitamin daily
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; postpartum OB visit in 6 weeks; general surgery in 6 to 8 weeks for interval laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Low-fat diet until then. Return for fever, worsening abdominal pain, jaundice, heavy bleeding or wound redness.

conditions.label: Acquired absence of uterus and cervix
conditions.note: Cesarean hysterectomy for placenta accreta, ovaries conserved

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 3 days after discharge from the tertiary center. Records reviewed.

Summary: Listeria bacteremia 6/3 treated with 14 days of ampicillin (finished 6/16, PICC out). Then acute calculous cholecystitis 6/17 at 35 weeks; with the accreta, delivery was moved up and she had a cesarean hysterectomy 6/19, ovaries kept, EBL 1.6 L, no transfusion. Baby girl in the NICU for observation, doing well, expected home next week. Gallbladder to come out electively in August.

Today: sore at the incision, walking more each day. No fever. Eating a low-fat diet, no RUQ pain since discharge. Finishing amoxicillin-clavulanate tomorrow. Using acetaminophen around the clock, ibuprofen a couple of times a day, and her usual 1-2 oxycodone; has not needed more. Mood: tired, emotional at times, but feels supported. PHQ-9 4. Bleeding light.

Exam: Vitals as charted, afebrile. Well appearing. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen: Pfannenstiel incision clean and dry, healing, appropriately tender; RUQ nontender, Murphy negative. Calves soft.

A/P:
1. S/p cesarean hysterectomy for placenta accreta - recovering as expected. CBC today. OB postpartum visit 7/31.
2. Acute calculous cholecystitis - improved; finish antibiotic; interval lap chole with surgery in August.
3. Maternal listeriosis - treated, course complete. Resolved.
4. Chronic low back pain - oxycodone unchanged, #90/30 days, PDMP reviewed. No additional opioid.
5. Mood - screen low; reviewed postpartum depression warning signs, she will reach out.
Follow up after the cholecystectomy.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count is coming back up after surgery, hemoglobin is already up a little from the 10.4 they found in the hospital, and your white count is normal, so no sign of ongoing infection. Eat well, keep up the prenatal vitamin, and we'll recheck in August.

documents.title: Obstetrics: postpartum visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Obstetrics and Gynecology
Postpartum visit 7/31/2025, 6 weeks after cesarean hysterectomy

Recovering well. Baby home from the NICU and feeding well. Minimal incisional discomfort. No bleeding. No fever. Mood good, sleeping when the baby sleeps, good support at home.

Exam: Pfannenstiel incision well healed. Speculum: vaginal cuff healing well, no discharge or granulation tissue. Bimanual: no masses or tenderness.

Assessment: normal postpartum recovery after cesarean hysterectomy for placenta accreta. Ovaries conserved, no hormone replacement needed. No further cervical screening needed given total hysterectomy for a benign indication with prior normal screening.
Plan: may resume full activity and lifting as tolerated; pelvic rest for 2 more weeks. Return as needed.
Obstetrics

reports.text: Specimen: gallbladder, laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Gross: gallbladder 7.5 cm in length, opened to reveal multiple yellow faceted stones; wall mildly thickened. Microscopic: chronic inflammatory infiltrate of the wall with Rokitansky-Aschoff sinuses; no dysplasia or malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Chronic cholecystitis with cholelithiasis. Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.

documents.title: Operative report: laparoscopic cholecystectomy
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
General Surgery, regional hospital
Date of surgery: 8/12/2025

Preoperative diagnosis: cholelithiasis, status post acute calculous cholecystitis in June treated with antibiotics.
Procedure: laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
Anesthesia: general.

Findings: Healed Pfannenstiel incision. Gallbladder without acute inflammation. Critical view of safety obtained. Cystic duct and artery clipped and divided. Gallbladder removed intact in a retrieval bag through the umbilical port.
Estimated blood loss: minimal. Complications: none.

Discharged home the same day, tolerating diet. Acetaminophen and ibuprofen for pain; she will use her own oxycodone if needed, no new opioid prescribed. Follow up in clinic in 2 weeks.

Pathology (8/14): chronic cholecystitis with cholelithiasis, benign.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks out from lap chole, eight weeks from the hysterectomy. Feels like herself again. Port sites healed, eating normally, no abdominal pain. Back pain is back to baseline, 4/10, carrying the baby is the hard part. Still 1-2 oxycodone a day. Mood good, PHQ-9 3. Planning to go back to work part-time in September.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight trending down. Abdomen soft, nontender, port sites and Pfannenstiel incision healed. Back unchanged.

A/P:
- S/p cesarean hysterectomy and laparoscopic cholecystectomy, recovered. Pathology benign. CBC today to confirm recovery of hemoglobin.
- Right thyroid nodule: ENT FNA visit is 9/23 as planned.
- Otosclerosis: ENT will repeat hearing test at the same visit.
- Chronic low back pain: continue oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn #90, PDMP reviewed.
- Occupational exposure: she will ask her employer's occupational health office for the safety data sheets before returning.
Flu and COVID in October.

reports.text: Comparison: 11/21/2024. Right lobe solid nodule measures 2.0 cm in greatest dimension, unchanged, with the same microcalcifications and irregular margins. Left lobe and isthmus without nodules. No cervical lymphadenopathy. Ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration of the right nodule performed, 25-gauge needle, three passes, no complications.
reports.conclusion: Unchanged 2.0 cm suspicious right thyroid nodule. FNA performed.

reports.text: Specimen: right thyroid nodule, ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration. Adequacy: satisfactory, with sufficient follicular cell groups. Cytology: benign-appearing follicular cells in macrofollicular and flat sheets with colloid; no nuclear features of papillary carcinoma.
reports.conclusion: Benign (Bethesda category II), consistent with a benign follicular nodule.

reports.text: Pure-tone air and bone conduction both ears with masking. Right ear: conductive hearing loss, unchanged from February 2025. Left ear: within normal limits. Word recognition excellent bilaterally.

orders.order: Thyroid ultrasound with repeat fine-needle aspiration, 12 months
orders.reason: Benign cytology in a high-suspicion right thyroid nodule

documents.title: Otolaryngology: thyroid FNA and hearing
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Otolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
Date of service: 9/23/2025

Dear Doctor,
Ms. Richard returned now that she has recovered from delivery (cesarean hysterectomy for accreta in June) and an interval cholecystectomy in August.

Thyroid: No neck symptoms. Ultrasound today shows the right nodule unchanged at 2.0 cm with the same suspicious features, and no abnormal nodes. We performed ultrasound-guided FNA. Cytology returned benign (Bethesda II), a benign follicular nodule. Because the sonographic pattern is high suspicion, a benign result does not fully settle it, and our plan is a repeat ultrasound with repeat FNA in 12 months, in September 2026. Surgery was discussed as an alternative; she prefers surveillance.

Hearing: Her hearing has not improved after delivery. Audiogram again shows a right conductive loss, stable compared with February. We talked through a hearing aid versus stapes surgery. She would like to start with a hearing aid; referral placed to audiology.

Regards,
Otolaryngology

documents.title: Fall vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 2025-26 trivalent flu 0.5 mL IM right deltoid, Pfizer 2025-26 COVID 0.3 mL IM left deltoid. No fever, no prior reactions. Back at work three days a week. Tolerated well, left after 15 minutes.

documents.title: Thyroid biopsy
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ENT said my biopsy was benign but they still want to do it again next year. Is that normal? I thought benign meant done.

documents.title: RE: Thyroid biopsy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. The biopsy was benign, which is good news. The reason for repeating it is that the nodule's ultrasound appearance is the kind where a needle sample can occasionally miss something, so the standard approach is to look again with ultrasound and repeat the biopsy in about a year. It's a safety check, not a sign they think something is wrong. I'll keep an eye on it with you.

documents.title: Audiology: hearing aid fitting
documents.author: audiology
documents.body:
Audiology
Date of service: 11/6/2025

Referred by ENT for amplification of a right conductive hearing loss from otosclerosis. Audiogram from 9/23/2025 reviewed.

Fitted today with a right behind-the-ear hearing aid, programmed to her thresholds and verified with real-ear measurement. Care, cleaning, battery charging and phone streaming reviewed. She noticed an immediate difference with speech in the room.

Plan: 30-day trial period, follow-up adjustment in 3 to 4 weeks.
Audiology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
29 y/o for annual exam. Last physical May 2024; last year was taken up by the pregnancy.

Interval: June 2025 Listeria bacteremia at 33 weeks, then acute calculous cholecystitis at 35 weeks, with delivery moved up to a cesarean hysterectomy for placenta accreta (ovaries conserved), then interval lap chole in August. All recovered. Daughter is 8 months and well. Back to work four days a week.

Ongoing:
- Chronic low back pain: 3-4/10, oxycodone 1-2 a day, agreement current.
- Right thyroid nodule: FNA 9/2025 benign; ENT repeating ultrasound and FNA in September.
- Right otosclerosis: right hearing aid since November, happy with it.
- Occupational: she reviewed the safety data sheets with her occupational health office and uses the hood and gloves for the solvent work.

Meds: oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn. Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol. Walking with the stroller most days.
PHQ-9 2, GAD-7 2.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight close to pre-pregnancy. Ears: right hearing aid in place, canals and TMs normal. Neck: firm right thyroid nodule, unchanged, no adenopathy. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen: healed Pfannenstiel and laparoscopic port scars, soft, nontender. Back and neuro unchanged.

Plan:
- CBC, CMP, TSH today.
- Cervical screening no longer needed after total hysterectomy for a benign reason with normal prior Paps.
- Vaccines up to date (flu and COVID 10/2025, Tdap 4/2025).
- Back pain: continue current plan. We talked again about trying a lower dose; she'd like to wait until the baby is sleeping through the night. Will revisit in the summer.
RTC 3 months.
